data.name: Murano Glass Museum Entrance Tickets
data.shortDescription:
The Murano Glass Museum was founded in 1861 when the darkest period in the history of Murano glassmaking had been overcome, following the fall of the Republic of San Marco ( 1797) and the subsequent years of foreign rule.

The Murano Glass Museum collection is laid out chronologically on the first floor of the museum. Starting from an archaeological section on the ground floor, which contains noteworthy Roman works dating from the 1st to the 3rd century A.D., it follows to the largest historical collection of Murano glass in the world, with pieces dating from the 15th to the 20th century, many of them world-famous masterpieces.

data.name: The Magic of Dolomites: Alpine Adventure
data.description: Experience the Alps & Dolomites Fantasia tour, a 5-day adventure that immerses you in the breathtaking beauty and rich culture of northern Italy. Begin your journey in Cortina d'Ampezzo, often acknowledged as the "Queen of the Dolomites," where the majestic peaks of the mountains create a backdrop of stunning natural beauty. Day 1: Mestre · Asolo · Valdobbiadene and the Prosecco Road · Cortina Your adventure starts with a visit to the picturesque medieval village of Asolo, known as the "city with a hundred horizons." Explore its historic center, including landmarks like Piazza Garibaldi, the Castle housing Teatro Duse, and the ancient Cathedral with Lorenzo Lotto's "Assumption" painting. Afterwards, embark on a scenic drive through the Prosecco region, an area universally known for its sparkling wine. Visit a traditional winery, unlock the secrets of Prosecco production, and indulge in a wine tasting session paired with local cold cuts and cheeses. Continue your drive to Cortina d'Ampezzo, where you'll spend the night. Day 2: Cortina · Scenic Drive Around the Lakes near Cortina · Lake Misurina · Lake Dobbiaco · San Vito di Cadore · Cortina Start your day with an energetic breakfast and prepare for a day of exploration. Marvel at the iconic Tre Cime di Lavaredo and take in the majestic mountain vistas of the Dolomite valley. Visit Lake Misurina, the largest natural lake in the region, and admire its captivating mountain views. Next, explore Lake Dobbiaco, known for its uniquely emerald-colored waters. Your journey continues to San Vito di Cadore, a picturesque mountain village with UNESCO-listed peaks in the background. Return to Cortina for free time to explore or relax. Day 3: Cortina · Lake Braies (Pragser Wildsee) or Lake Anterselva · Brunico · Bressanone · Bolzano Today, your first stop is the captivating Lake Braies, also known as Pragser Wildsee, nestled amidst the Dolomite Mountains. Alternatively, you may visit Lake Anterselva, a hidden gem with its unique charm. Explore the charming town of Brunico, a blend of Alpine tradition and Italian charm, before making a stop in Bressanone, known for its vineyards and medieval cathedral. Reach Bolzano for the overnight stay. Day 4: Bolzano · Merano · Vipiteno · Bolzano Discover the charms of Merano, known for its enchanting Christmas market and cultural heritage. Explore the old town and savor local flavors during lunch. Continue your journey to Vipiteno, a charming town with Alpine allure. Wander through its historic center, shop for souvenirs, and enjoy Alpine cuisine. Return to Bolzano, a vibrant city blending Alpine and Mediterranean influences, and explore its cultural attractions. Day 5: Bolzano · Kaltern an der Weinstraße (scenic drive) · Egna · Trento · Milan Embark on a journey along the oldest Italian wine route, winding through vineyards and idyllic villages. Visit the charming village of Egna and experience South Tyrolean traditions. Explore Trento, a city with historical treasures and architectural gems. Your tour concludes in the vibrant city of Milan

data.name: Enchanting Venice - Private Gondola Experience
data.description: The gondola is one of the main symbols of Venice, as emblematic of the famous water city as mysterious in its origins. Not many people know that at the beginning this unique vessel was different from the one we can admire today, changing across time together with the city it is associated to. Of course, the history of the gondola is deeply bounded to the one of Venice. Considered one of the most beautiful and elegant boats on Earth, it is built through unique techniques and each part of it also has symbolic meanings. For example, its multi-pronged ferro, or prow, does have five or six “pettini”, symbolic of the six “sestieri” in which Venice is divided into. The function of this part made of iron is to balance gondoliere’s weigh and it has an “S” shape evoking the flow of the Canal Grande. Not only elegance and beauty then, a whole world embodied into this boat nowadays symbol of Venice. Let yourself experience in first person the gondola through this tour. An enchanting and relaxing way to enjoy the colors, lights, sights, charm and beauty of Venice. You will admire elegant bank-side palaces, unique bridges and breath the charming and magic atmosphere that only a town built on water can give you. Can you imagine a better experience to share with the people you love? Probably difficult to find. Just take your smile and beloved one with you, the timeless beauty of Venice seen from the gondola will do the rest

data.name: Lords of the Night Prison Palace: tour to the cells and torture tools
data.description: Discover the secret itinerary in the mysterious Prisons of Piazza San Marco, connected to the Doge’s Palace by the Bridge of Sighs.The Palace is "populated" by life-size figures of the Lords of the Night, prisoners, Judges, Lawyers and all the characters who worked in the Prisons, painstakingly drawn from ancient manuscripts. The guide will bring you through exclusive places: you will have the opportunity to enter the torture room and see authentic torment items used by the torturers in the past to make the criminals confess. There, you will discover the stories about the Lords of the Nights: the terrible Venetian police who oversaw the crimes and brought criminals and betrayers in front of the courtroom.You will go down to the cold cells to see the lifestyle of the prisoners: what they ate, drank and where they slept. Here you can also admire the original graffiti left by the prisoners and listen about the thrilling Casanova’s escape: he managed to evade from the maximum-security jail known as “Piombi”!You will discover the alternative that prisoners had between staying in a cell or serving their sentence on board a Venetian galley. Each year of boarding as a Galeotti was worth the same as spending 2 years in a cell.Listen to the histories and legends that still reside inside these cells and halls. Along the itinerary, you’ll enjoy the explanation of the powerful “Council of The Ten”, composed by the highest Venice Politicians that ran the justice in all Venetian domains.

data.name: St. Mark's Basilica 3-Hour Skip-the-Line Walking and Boat Tour
data.description:
Start your "Venice in a day" tour with a guided walk to learn about the city’s key monuments. In St. Mark’s Square, hear the history behind legendary sights such as St. Mark’s Basilica and the Doge’s Palace prisons.

Admission lines at top Venice attractions are long and no more so than at St. Mark’s Basilica. Use your skip-the-line ticket to bypass the lines and step straight inside. Then admire the acclaimed mosaics that adorn the basilica’s interior as you explore with your guide.

From St. Mark’s Basilica, continue to Campo Santa Maria Formosa to admire from outside the stunning Renaissance church dedicated to the Holy Virgin and learn from your guide the meaning of "formosa".

Leave the tourist crowds behind, and follow your guide around the winding alleyways that form the backstreets of Hidden Venice and Castello district. Explore narrow passageways that cut between sun-bleached palazzos, and admire the bridges that cross the canals.

Pass through Campo Santa Maria Formosa to see its gothic palaces, and have your camera ready for Marco Polo’s House. Other sights include Calle del Paradiso, San Zulian, an age-old merchants warehouse and a wellhead, which many say is the city’s most beautiful.

Say goodbye to your guide at St Mark's Square, and make the most of some free time before your water taxi cruise along the Grand Canal.

As you glide down the waterway, listen to stories about the eye-catching palaces and churches that line your route, pass by Rialto bridge, and hear fun facts about the famous residents that have lived on the equally famous street. Continue on a tour of the smaller, lesser-seen canals. Hop back on to dry land to finish your experience in central Venice.

Please note: There is a break between the walking tour and Grand Canal boat tour, for you to spend time at leisure. The duration of this break varies depending on the season. Details of the exact meeting location and time for the Grand Canal Boat Tour are given by your meeting point assistant upon check-in for the first tour.

data.name: Cicchetti & Wine: Private 2-hour Food Tour in Venice
data.description: Enjoy a gastronomical experience of Venetian Cicchetti and wine ‘Ombra’ on this foodie tour of Venice. On your private food tour, you will: Enjoy the personalised attention of a private tour guide and local foodie expert who will be able to customise this tour to best match your taste buds and interests; Meet your guide at your hotel and explore the surrounding area on this delicious food-tasting tour; Get acquainted with the local food options in three different Cicchetti (Venetian Tapas) bars; At each stop enjoy a curated selection of two Cicchetti, your guide will be sure to point out local favourites; Savour specialities such as baccalàmantecato (salt cod on grilled polenta), sardeinsaor (sardines in sweet and sour vinegar sauce), polpette (meatballs) or a variety of mouth-watering mini sandwiches; Learn why a glass of wine is called an "Ombra" or shadow in Venice, and practice ordering one at each of the three locations;  Step away from the beaten tourist paths and discover the local side of Venice, through its food and most charming bars. Enjoy wandering around beautiful Venice with your expert, English-speaking private guide on this gastronomic foodie tour of some of the best Cicchetti bars in this unique city on the water. Cicchetti is a whole culture in Venice, and can be found on almost every street! Cicchetti refers to plates of tasty small eats like Spanish tapas that can be enjoyed as appetizers or even a meal. Cicchetti is eaten casually – with fingers and toothpicks, usually standing up by the counter or at tall outdoor tables, and often enjoyed with a small glass of wine that the locals call an ‘Ombra’ meaning shadow. On your private tour, your guide will tailor your route according to your preferences and hotel location. Discover several different taverns popular with the locals, but off the tourist trail, that serve delicious classics Cicchetti and Ombra. You’ll stop in three different places, sample different dishes and be able to soak up the authentic Venetian atmosphere! Venetian food is unlike food anywhere else in Italy – with its long history of trading, the food here makes extensive use of exotic spices, while its watery location means fish is on the menu more often than not. Venice can make a fantastic break from the usual pizza-and-pasta gastronomy of Italy, but with so many touristy restaurants on the island, it can be hard to make the most of Venetian cuisine and wine on your own. On this private-guide-led exploration of Venice’s most bustling markets, cafés, and its famous Cicchetti bars, you will delve into an authentic side of Venetian culture, learning what to order, how to find great places and enjoying lots of tastings along the way – so make sure you have a hearty appetite before you join us!

data.name: Venice in the Middle Ages: Documents and Torture Instruments
data.shortDescription: Discover documents and objects that marked the years of Venetian Republic
data.description:
Suggestive testimonies, documents and objects: these are just some of the elements that combine to make Maleficia a unique exhibition, capable of revealing the mysteries, secrets, legends, and historical facts that marked the thousand extraordinary years of the Serenissima Republic. 

Journey inside the prestigious Prisons' Palace and see original artifacts and reproductions of ancient documents used by the Holy Office in the persecution of witchcraft, and the instruments of brutal justice employed to counter it. 

In this palace, between the 15th and 18th centuries, the terrible Tribunal of the Inquisition condemned to death many women accused of dabbling in evil spells, magical arts and the occult. 

Discover instruments of torture like an original garrote, a head crusher, and an authentic whipping post in this special exhibition of medieval superstition and suffering.

data.name: Explore Murano, the Island of Glass & Colour: Private Tour by Boat
data.description: Experience the iconic archipelago of Murano, world-famous for its glassmaking, by private water taxi. On your private tour you will: Enjoy the personal attention of your private guide with pick up and drop off at the location of your choice in central Venice; Travel by luxury Venetian motorboat, the most comfortable and coolest way to reach the island of Murano; Learn why Murano is the centrefor glassmaking in Venice and Europe; Visit Murano's oldest glassmaking factory, famous for its expertise in the working of Venetian Chandeliers exhibited in acclaimed museums all over the world;  See firsthand a glass-making demonstration by the Master glassblower himself or one of his trusted assistants; Visit an exclusive exhibition normally closed to the public, and meet a world-acclaimed Master glassblower; Travel like a local, and enjoy a luxury boat ridethrough the Venetian Lagoon with stunning panoramic views. The Venetian Lagoon has many islands, each with its own character and heritage. Foremost among these is the archipelago of Murano, with its many bridges connecting the islands, which provides a respite from the touristy bustle of the historic city. Murano has been the centre of glassmaking in the region since 1291. Your tour guide will take you via private water taxi across the stunning Venetian Lagoon to Murano. On arrival, you'll walk the colourful streets and enjoy many photo opportunities before enjoying an exclusive visit to the oldest family-run glass workshop, not usually open to the public. Here you'll meet the master glassblower and his team who will give you a private demonstration in which you'll see how they twist the molten glass to make different shapes and items. If you are lucky, you will also see them colouring the glass. A very special part of the tour includes a private viewing of the world-famous Maestro Fabio Fornasier's exhibition, not open to the general public. Throughout the experience, your guide will explain the history and secrets of the profession, how glassblowing shaped the fabric of Murano’s society and odd little facts such as why the glassblowers used to be immune from prosecution.

data.name: St. Mark’s Basilica & Doge’s Palace Half-Day Tour with Gondola Ride
data.description: The excitement of planning a visit to Venice can become a challenge due to crowds and long waits. Our expert guides grant you privileged entrance, allowing you to skip the lines at St. Mark’s Basilica and the Doge’s Palace. Next, it's time to relax as your guide will then lead you to the serene waters of the Grand Canal on a classic gondola ride, capturing the essence of this enchanting city in just a few hours. Without the hassle, our guides get you where you need to be with time to spare.Tour OverviewYou’ll meet up with your local guide and the rest of your group in the famous St. Mark’s Square near the two columns by the canal. Skip the long lines at St. Mark’s so you can get right inside to learn about this magnificent golden church. Then explore the Doge’s Palace where you’ll see the golden staircase, prisons, and Bridge of Sighs. Finally, your guide will escort you to your gondola ride that might just become your favorite activity of the day! Each gondola seats up to 5 guests and is shared exclusively with fellow travelers from your group—offering a more intimate and comfortable way to enjoy Venice’s canals without the crowds.St. Mark’s, Doge’s Palace, and Gondola Tour DescriptionYour 3.5-hour tour includes:Skip-the-line entry and guided tour of St. Mark’s BasilicaSkip-the-line entry and guided tour of Doge’s Palace30-minute gondola ride ( max 5 people shared experience)Maximum group size of 20A local, English-speaking guideSt. Mark’s BasilicaYou’ll begin your tour of Venice in St. Mark's Square, or Piazza San Marco, which is perhaps one of the most famous public squares in the world. Then follow your guide past the crowds for your skip-the-line entry into St. Mark’s Basilica to see why it’s nicknamed the “Church of Gold”. With over 45,000 square feet of gilded mosaics constructed over eight centuries, the interior of St. Mark's Basilica is unlike anything you've ever seen.Please note that St. Mark's is a sacred place, so we ask both men and women to cover knees and shoulders, otherwise you might be refused entry and you’ll miss out on a portion of your tour. We understand the summers in Venice can be hot, so a great alternative is to bring a shawl/scarf/sweater with you. That way you can cover your knees and shoulders when necessary.Doge’s Palace and Bridge of SighsThe Gothic building right next to St. Mark’s Basilica is the infamous Doge’s Palace that has a storied past of tyranny, torture, and an iron fist of rulers. From the 15th to 18th centuries, the Doges of Venice lived and ruled from this palace that includes paintings from Titian, Tintoretto, and Veronese.The interior of the Doge's Palace is grand to say the least. Inside you’ll find marble fireplaces, friezes and stucco adorning the walls. Some works of art stand out over the rest, including iconic pieces by Titian, Tintoretto, and Veronese, and your guide will explain the stories and interpretations behind the art. You'll also pass through the awe-inspiring Great Council Chamber, which is one of the largest rooms in Europe and the place where the most important decisions were discussed.One of the palace's most impressive features is the Golden Staircase, considered the most valuable staircase ever built. It connects the first floor of the palace to the third, where the Doge's offices were located. Your guide will show you the grand offices from which Venice was ruled for centuries, including the rooms that housed the powerful Council of Ten—the city's governing body.Linking the palace to the prison cells, you'll cross the infamous Bridge of Sighs (Ponte dei Sospiri). Prisoners walked across this enclosed bridge before spending years or even the remainder of their lives behind bars. If that wasn’t enough to sigh about, look out from the small windows carved into the bridge that once offered convicts their last glimpse of beautiful Venice. That's plenty to sigh about.Enjoy a Gondola Ride—Just for Your Tour Group!As part of your experience, you’ll enjoy a 30-minute gondola ride through Venice’s iconic canals. Each gondola holds up to 5 guests and will be shared only with others from your tour group—never with random travelers. This allows you to soak in the beauty of Venice from the water in a more intimate, relaxed setting, all while keeping the experience affordable and authentic.Being an island and subject to problems related to high water, the gondola or boat tour cannot be guaranteed due to force majeure.

data.name: 3 hours Venice walking tour
data.description: Discover the hidden gems of the UNESCO World Heritage Site of Venice on this action-packed walking tour. With its narrow streets and 400 bridges, it can be easy to get lost in Venice, but you won’t have to worry about navigating, as a guide will lead the way. data.name: Carnival Masks & Gondola's Workshops: Private Tour in Venice
data.description: Immerse yourself in the backstreet world of artisanal Venice on this three-hour tour, where you’ll learn about the making of the oldest Venetian traditional crafts - from the gondolas to the masks. On your private tour, you will: Enjoy the personal attention of your private guide as they expertly navigate you through the city’s lesser-known alleys and backwaters; Discover the oldest crafts of Venice, visit a collection of Venetian workshops, and meet the artisans; Visit a gondola workshop and meet the “Squerariòl” carpenter who specializes in the construction of wooden boats, including the gondola; Chat with a ‘Remer, who makes oars, and marvel at the specialized carpentry involved; Meet a “Mascarer” craftsman and watch as he demonstrates how to make a colourful Venetian Carnival mask; Explore the most ancient weaving factory in Venice and learn of rich the tradition of textile craft and trade in Venice; Finish the tour at the atelier of the last local woodcarver and gain a true appreciation for the intricately crafted wooden decorations found throughout Venice, such as the ceilings of the Accademia or the choir in Santa Maria Gloriosa dei Frari; This quintessential Venetian experience is ideal for travellers looking to go behind the façade of the city and learn about the artisans who have made the city famous. You will meet the incredibly skilled craftspeople who have for generations made the gondolas, the masks, the costumes and all the fine things that Venice is world-renowned for. Enjoy a walk with your local, English-speaking private guide through the traditional districts of the city, and visit a collection of Venetian artisans' workshops located in the lesser-known back alleys of Venice. You’ll visit the workshops of gondola makers, mask makers, and weavers and learn about the intricacies of carving the oars and rowlocks. You’ll be treated to a demonstration of how to make a Carnival mask – and observe the colourful precision involved in each hand-made piece. The tour concludes with a visit to an ancient weaving factory and to the atelier of the last local woodcarver. data.name: Soave and Valpolicella Wine Route from Venice
data.description: After you meet the tour driver in Venice, you will be brought along the famous Soave and Valpolicella Wine Route. Amarone della Valpolicella is made with local grapes Corvina, Corvinone, Rondinella generally picked (barring anomalous weather conditions) between the end of September and beginning of October. In order to successfully complete the critical phase of "appassimento" (drying process), the fruit must be fully ripe and in perfect condition, therefore the fruit selection in the vineyard is very accurate..  You will be introduced to these wines in a morning visit to the first local winery. A luscious, typical lunch will be followed by a visit to the second winery. Sipping wine and tasting local products, you’ll learn about the different techniques of viticulture. data.name: Venice: Classic Gondola Ride
data.description:
In a city with no roads, boats rule supreme. Locals might favor motors, but everyone needs to experience Venice by gondola at least once. Sit back and feel your cares melt away as your stripy-shirted gondolier glides you through a maze of waterways, before joining the central Grand Canal.

This once-in-a-lifetime experience just asks for a perfect picture. Luckily for you, with just five other people on board (including the gondolier), you have more than enough space for a selfie.

Don’t be surprised if you attract a little envy on this voyage. Most tourists easily part with a hundred bucks for a short gondola ride, while you’ll be parading over the water for a pittance. But that’s our secret… _shhh_!

Visit the Gondola Gallery to learn how Venice’s famous boats are made. See original tools, a gondola cross-section, and examples of traditional craftsmanship. Then, take a virtual gondola ride through the canals of Venice and learn about the city’s history and traditions.

data.name: The Doge's Palace of Venice: Private 2.5-hour Walking Tour
data.description: Discover the fascinating history of Venice by exploring the magnificent Doge’s Palace (in Italian Palazzo Ducale), the former residence of the Doge of Venice and one of the most popular attractions in the heart of the city with a private tour guide. The Venetian Gothic Style 14th-century building became a museum in 1923 and visiting its rooms is the best way to learn about the past of "La Serenissima". On your private tour you will: Meet your guide in St. Mark's Square, for an introduction to the area before entering the Doge's Palace; Explore the Doge's Palace as you learn about the sophisticated government systems of the Venetian Republic, also known as "The Most Serene Republic of Venice"; Get acquainted with the Doge's of Venice, elected for life, these chief magistrates were the leaders of the Republic for over 1000 years; See the apartment rooms where the Dogesresided while in power, and learn of their way of life and beliefs; Take in the magnificent Giants' (Scala dei Giganti) and Golden (Scala d'Oro) staircases, ceremonial masterpieces of their times, built respectively in the 15th and 16th centuries; Explore the opulent government rooms, including the Venetian Senate Hall that could accommodate up to 200 people, the CollegioHall with ceiling breathtaking decorations by Veronese, and Tintoretto's "Paradise" painting, believed to be the world’s largest canvas painting, in the Grand Council Hall; Cross the Bridge of Sighs, which connects the interrogation rooms at the Doge's Palace with the New Prison, and learn how this famous bridge got its name; End your tour with a visit to the dark prison cells where you will learn of the strict justice system of the Serenissima, which considered itself incorruptible and utterlyimpartial. There is no better way to understand the power which Venice had over the overworld than by a private, guided tour of Doge’s Palace. For over a thousand years beginning in the eighth century, Venice was ruled by doges – elected magistrates who served for life. While the process for selecting doges changed throughout the millennium, the singular law was simply that no doge could pass his title on to a member of his own family. While the original wood structure burned down, the building which stands today is still a staggering 700 years old. From its ornate wood carvings to its larger-than-life facades, the palace is more than just a historical sight – it’s an architectural masterpiece and a visual feast. Whilst touring the palace, see works by Titian, Tintoretto, and Tiepolo amongst others.

data.name: Secret Venice: Palazzo Grimani and hidden corners of Venice
data.description: This tour will take you to some of the most fascinating, yet lesser known attractions in Venice, such as “Palazzo Grimani”, St. Maria Formosa’s church and the ‘Acqua Alta’ bookshop. The itinerary is designed to explore the city off the beaten path, walking through alleys and small bridges across the ‘sestiere’ of Castello, one of the least tourist neighborhoods in Venice. You will discover “Palazzo Grimani” (Grimani Palace), former residence of the patrician Grimani family, which has recently been renovated and open to the public as a ‘residence-museum’. The most spectacular room of the palace is the Tribune, the sculpture gallery, featuring stands and niches set in the wall to display some of the finest statues and busts, which were part of one of the largest art collections in the sixteenth-century Venice. Not far from “Palazzo Grimani”, you will be walking through some of the best-preserved medieval lanes, across pointed arches and cobbled streets, the foundations of which were laid many centuries ago. While strolling around in a maze of narrow lanes, you will be heading to Campo Santa Maria Formosa, one of the largest and most lively squares in the city. The landmark of this prominent setting is Santa Maria Formosa Church, the first church in Venice dedicated to the Virgin Mary in the 7th century A.D. Just around the corner from Santa Maria Formosa, strolling down streets that are easily overlooked, you will discover a hidden place where you will be thrown back in time. It is the peculiar ‘Acqua Alta’ bookshop, an international bookselling place where piles of volumes are stored on ad-hoc shelves and versatile containers, in an attempt to withstand floods in times of high tide. It is a place where you are literally surrounded by heaps of books in an otherworldly atmosphere, which reminds you of the fairy tales and ghost stories taking place once upon a time. This is a rare opportunity for book lovers to find old and new publications, as well as for visitors to enjoy a peaceful reading spot away from the suffocating crowds. In a nutshell, Secret Venice tour is an excellent choice to discover Venice through alternative, yet spectacular walking paths

After experiencing the grandiosity and the opulence of the Doge’s Palace, you'll make your way to the imposing St. Mark's Basilica, the cathedral church of the Roman Catholic Diocese of Venice, and one of the best examples of Italo-Byzantine architecture.

data.name: Palazzo Fortuny: Entry Ticket
data.shortDescription: Immerse yourself in the customs and traditions of the ever prestigious Venice
data.description:
When you visit Venice, you can't miss Fortuny Palace, with its centuries worth of history. When you pass through the front door, you immerse yourself in the customs and traditions of Venice.

Its unique facade is characterised by seven openings, while its interior has wooden lintels and marble pillars. Its architectural beauty is what attracted the designer Mariano Fortuny, who decided to restore the palace and give it back its lost beauty.

Amongst the designer's creations, you can admire the winter garden and painting studio located on the first noble floor. The space features art of female figures, allegorical images, satyrs and exotic animals, parrots, and monkeys enveloped in floral and vegetable motifs, garlands and grotesques.

data.name: Venice Semi-Private Tour of Doge's Palace and Saint Mark's

data.name: The Doge's Palace (Skip the Line)
data.description: Since far back in time, a majestic building and architectural masterpiece greeted the ships coming from the lagoon: The Doge's Palace, the place where the Doge and his Council used to rule the Republic of the Serenissima. Today, the symbol of Venice and its power is still standing in all of its beauty and majesty, everyday taking travelers' breath away. A tour to discover the heart of Venice and its history, the charm of the past and a truly beautiful gem where inestimable art masterpieces are shielded The Doge’s Palace is one of the most important symbols of Venice. For centuries, it has represented the seat of the Venetian political power. In its majestic rooms, the Doge and his Council for centuries controlled the fate of the Serenissima surrounded by hundreds of masterpieces of painting art. Visiting its halls of power, gold staircases and the important paintings, we will have the opportunity to go back in time and breathe the charming atmosphere of the place where Byzantine and Orient architectures run into each other. Inside the Palace we will admire some of the most famous works painted by Tintoretto, Veronese and other important artists. Finally we will feel again the anguish of the prisoners, who after crossing the well-known Bridge of Sighs entered in the darkness of the prisons. Let's join this tour which will make us marvel in front of Doge's Palace's art masterpieces, its Golden Staircase, the Venetian prison which will reveal how the prisoners of the Serenissima used to live

data.name: Venice Carnival Tour of Must-See Sites with Local Guide & Frittelle Tasting
data.description: Venice is famed for its colorful Carnival, which is best experienced in the company of a guide who can explain its intricacies. This private tour, exclusively for your party, introduces you to the stories behind the masks and colorful costumes and immerses you fully in the festive atmosphere.

data.name: Day Trip by train from Venice to Padua. Private tour
data.description: Your tour at the discovery of one of the most enchanting cities in Veneto starts at 8.40 from the railway station of Venice Santa Lucia. Here you will take a speed train that will bring you to Padua in only 25 minutes. Your private guide will wait for you at Piazza Garibaldi, which can be easily reached with a pleasant 10 minute-walk or, in alternative, with public transport. In this cosy, tree-lined square the car-free area begins and so does your visit. Thanks to an expert guide you will discover the treasures of the Paduan historic centre, starting from Cafè Pedrocchi, a world- famous 18th century literary cafè, passing by Palazzo del Bo, the historic headquarter of the University of Padua, founded in 1222. Your tour goes on through the lively squares of the city, Piazza delle Erbe and Piazza della Frutta, separated by the elegant and majestic Palazzo della Ragione, former headquarter of the city court that houses the magnificent cycle of astrological-themed frescoes. Further ahead you will find the exquisite Piazza dei Signori and the Torre dell’orologio with the astrological clock. A stop by Piazza Duomo is unmissable, with the Romanesque-styled cathedral and the baptistery. You will walk through the narrow streets of the Jewish ghetto, with its picturesque glimpses. Finally, you will reach Prato della Valle, which is one of the largest and most suggestive squares in Europe. Last but not the least, you will stop by the Basilica del Santo, the symbol of the city, which houses the remains of Saint Anthony, patron of Padua. Here your guided tour comes to the end. After the sightseeing tour, treat yourselves to a refreshing lunch and have some free time. In the afternoon, we suggest you the visit to the Orto botanico of Padua, the most ancient botanic garden located in its original place and nominated World Heritage site by UNESCO. Your visit to the city of Padua ends at 18.53 at the railway station where you will be supposed to catch the speed train back to Venice

data.name: Venice Music Museum + Audio Guide
data.description:
Explore a cornerstone of Italian cultural history with an audio-guided visit to the Venice Music Museum. This extraordinary exhibition space inside the San Maurizio church is dedicated to the rich tradition of Italian violin making. The collection "Antonio Vivaldi and his time" by Maestro Artemio Versari takes you on a journey into the golden age of Italian violin making, telling the story of 18th-century Venetian music through pieces belonging to the various workshops or "schools" that made Italian manufacture famous throughout Europe.

While musical instruments are prized for their attractive shapes and decorations, very little is widely known about their construction, and the fine details that separate high-class craftsmanship from true works of art. With this audio-guided visit to the Venice Music Museum, you'll learn all about the master violin makers, like Antonio Stradivari, and how their distinctive traditional violin-making techniques have never been bested.

data.name: Museum of Medieval Torture Venice: Skip The Line Entry
data.description:
It's not often you would want skip-the-line prison access, but in the case of the fascinating Palazzo delle Prigioni it's actually quite handy!

Venice's 16th-century jail is part palace, part penitentiary. A guided tour includes the courtroom where small-time villains of the Venetian Republic were sentenced, and their lonely cells. You'll also explore places never opened before and enter the torture room to see the instruments used in the past to make criminals confess

See real graffiti left by prisoners, hear about myths, legends and daring escapes, and consider the lightless existence for those inside this mysterious relic.

data.name: Palazzo Pisani: Venice's Highest Rooftop Terrace
data.description:
Venice on Top at Palazzo Pisani is here to showcase the best views of Venice from the city's highest panoramic terrace.

At 31-meters high, the terrace of the Pisani Palace – now home to the Venice Conservatory – opens onto a breathtaking panorama with sweeping views of all of Venice and a large part of the lagoon.

data.name: St. Mark's Basilica & Doge's Palace: After-closing Entry + Guided Tour
data.description:
Explore St. Mark's Basilica and the Doge's Palace on a late afternoon tour. Meet at the winged lion statue in St. Mark's Square.

Begin the tour as the Doge's Palace closes for the day. See the rulers' apartments and frescoes by Veronese and Tintoretto in the Hall of the Great Council.

Learn about the art, the doge veiled in black, and how the Dukes rose to power. Visit the massive armory and prison cells, and walk the Bridge of Sighs from the inside.

After a short break, visit St. Mark's Basilica, now free from the daytime crowds, and admire its Byzantine beauty.

data.name: Museums of Islands (Museo delle Isole): Entry Ticket

Explore the art of Venetian lace-making from the 16th to the 20th centuries at the Lace Museum, then check out the largest collection of Murano glass in history at the Glass Museum.

data.name: Private Half Day Wine Tasting tour: Road Of The Doges
data.description:
The Veneto winemaking region, just north of Venice, started producing wine as early as the 1st century, during the early rule of the Roman Empire. Explore the region’s historic vines and varietals on this private tour.

Make your way to Piazzale Roma in central Venice, where you’ll meet your local driver and hop aboard an air-conditioned Mercedes minivan. Along the way to the town of Treviso, your driver will share interesting facts about Veneto’s history and wines.

You’ll arrive at a charming 17th-century villa nestled among the rolling hills and vineyards of in the scenic Lison-Pramaggiore region. Meet the host of the 50-year-old winery housed here and learn how regional climate and soil conditions are ideal for producing grapes for chardonnay, pinot grigio, merlot, and cabernet franc, plus other regional varietals.

Tour the on-site barrel rooms and learn about the winemaking process, and then head to a table on the winery’s scenic grounds for a personalized tasting. Sample several different wines, and enjoy appetizers like fresh bread and cheeses to complement the wine’s flavors. Before you leave, you’ll have a chance to purchase a bottle or two to take home from the on-site wine shop. 

Relax on the scenic return drive to Venice, where you’ll be dropped off at the original departure point.

data.name: Padua: Guided Tour + Train Transfers from Venice + Botanical Garden Entry

data.name: Prosecco Wine Road: Full day tour and wine tasting from Venice
data.description: Come with us to a relaxing and slow full day tour of the Prosecco wine road and its region. Starting from Piazzale Roma, we will reach the Prosecco land by private car. This tour will take you directly to Valdobbiadene, a city well known for its wonderful wine yard and super tasting wines. Here, at about 11.30am we will reach the first winery where you will have your first wine tasting. Experts say that, this is the perfect time to taste some wine, since your body is at its top ready to welcome all the sensations wine can give you: from the nose sense of smell with its perfumes, to the brain. In the winery an expert will guide you first to see the winery itself and then to the cellar to explain the method of Prosecco making, from grape pickling to the fermentation. In the tasting room, we will enjoy some types of Prosecco (brut, extra dray, dray, cartizze or rosè) or other wines. For lunch we will take you to a wonderful restaurant overlooking wine yard: a spectacular scenery where to have a tasting lunch. (Lunch will be on your own expenses). After lunch, we will depart to Follina, in the province of Treviso. Here we will make a stop to see the wonderful abbey and its nearby cloister dated back on the XII century. Then the tour will continue with another tasting in another selected wine yard, where you could also see a wonderful wine yard and another different method of making the Prosecco. We will then reach Refrontolo, where you will see an old mill of the XVII century. After Refrontolo, we will head towards Venice, passing through the wonderful hills of Conegliano and Susegana.

data.name: St. Mark's Basilica: Skip The Line Ticket with Pala d’Oro Access

Inside, you’ll find more than 8,000 square meters of mosaics, many made with real gold, showing scenes from the Bible and Venice’s past. At the center of the church, you can see the Pala d’Oro, a 10th-century altarpiece decorated with nearly 2,000 gems and fine gold work.

data.name: Shared gondola ride with passage underneath the Bridge of Sighs
data.description: Step aboard the legendary Venetian gondola for an unforgettable journey, gliding through the most enchanting canals of Venice and passing underneath the iconic Bridge of Sighs, an architectural masterpiece that weaves together history, romance and a touch of melancholy. Legend has it that the Bridge of Sighs earned its name from the bittersweet sighs of prisoners who caught, crossing the famous bridge, a last glimpse of Venice’s breathtaking beauty before entering the prisons for good. Settle into your seat, and let be guided by a local gondolier in his iconic striped shirt. Drift along the hidden narrow canals on this leisurely 25/30 minute ride, immersing yourself in the city’s alluring secrets. Savor the unhurried pace of the gondola, allowing yourself to be embraced by the serenity of the experience. This is a slow ride, ensuring you to have ample time to soak in the atmosphere and truly appreciate the beauty that surrounds you, from the moment you step on board to the one you disembark. ABOUT THE GONDOLA: Regarded as one of the most exquisite and graceful vessels in existence, the Venetian gondola is steeped in rich tradition and craftmanship. Constructed using unique techniques, these magnificent boats hold deep symbolic meaning, like the gondola’s intricately designed ferro (or prow) with its multi-pronged shape. Known as pettini, these prongs symbolize the six divisions, or Sestieri, of Venice. Crafted from iron, the “ferro” serves a dual purpose: it provides balance to the gondoliers and evokes the graceful flow of the Grand Canal’s waters, capturing in its elegant S shape the essence of Venice’s fluidity. Allow yourself to be swept away on this enchanting voyage, where you will have the opportunity to traverse unique bridges, line the famous Bridge of Sighs, behold the splendor of elegant canal-side palaces and bask in the magical ambiance that can only be found here in Venice. With each passing moment, the beauty of Venice will unfold before your eyes.

data.name: Carlo Scarpa in Venice: where light and water become protagonists of architectural space
data.description: Carlo Scarpa (1906-1978) was one of the most influential architects in the 20th-century Italy, who skillfully interpreted Venice’s traditional architecture from a modern perspective. Since his early career, as artistic designer for Cappellin and Venini glass makers in Murano, Carlo Scarpa began to explore the vast potential of glass. By resuming ancient handcrafting processes and trying new glass blowing techniques, he developed chromatic and geometric solutions that changed Italian glass production forever. Since then, an innovative use of traditional raw materials has remained a distinctive feature of his works. In Venice’s urban context, where buildings and residences are reflected on the canals and the surrounding lagoon, water and light become an integral part of the environment. Carlo Scarpa decided to use natural elements, such as water and light, as architectural components, so to open spaces to perspective sceneries and infinite games of light. The first destination of the tour is the Olivetti Showroom in St. Mark’s Square. This is a modern example of interaction between inner and outer space in architecture. The showroom recreates the theme of water by using a few decoration ‘devices’: a trickle of water flowing down in an ornamental fountain on the ground floor; tiny colored glass tiles covering the floor, so that it reflects the light by producing the flickering water effect that characterizes the surface of St Mark’s Square in times of high tide. Large windows flood the showroom with light that reverberates on the fountain’s water and the gray-purplish wall stucco. Floor colours gradually fade off, as the distance from the windows increases. The showroom is decorated using local materials, such as glass, marble, stone, and wood, which are beautifully juxtapposed to create a stylish ambience for the display of Olivetti typewriters. These machines from the 1950s and 1960s are therefore exhibited as if they were ‘jewels in a museum’. Carlo Scarpa’s search for harmony between natural elements and architectural space is best illustrated at Venice’s Querini Stampalia Foundation, which is the next destination of the tour. Carlo Scarpa reinforced the building and renovated both the entrance hall of the museum and the palace’s garden. He regained control over an open portion of the building, which had been left in disuse because of being regularly flooded. Carlo Scarpa raised the area from the ground floor and transformed it into a walkway for the palace’s visitors. Water entering the ground floor was contained by a parapet wall and channelled into the rear garden. Thanks to this solution, water acquires an aesthetic value, while harmoniously coexisting with the other architectural elements of the building. This modern revisitation of an ancient building makes the former Querini Stampalia residence a masterpiece of twentieth-century architecture. The idea behind Carlo Scarpa’s project still inspires the mission of Querini Stampalia Foundation: opening to dialogue with society by creating a space for interaction and cultural exchange between the peoples of Venice

data.shortDescription:

Ammira le viste dalla terrazza panoramica della barca e ascolta i commenti della tua guida. 

All'arrivo alla tua prima tappa, Murano, scopri perché l'isola è rinomata per le sue vetrerie con una visita gratuita a una vetreria locale. Guarda un abile artigiano durante una dimostrazione di lavorazione del vetro. Successivamente, avrai circa un'ora sull'isola per fare shopping in uno dei tanti negozi di vetro.

Successivamente, dirigiti verso Burano, nota per i suoi merletti e le case dai colori vivaci. Segui la tua guida nel cuore della città e avrai 2 ore di tempo libero per acquistare un buon pranzo, tipici aperitivi veneziani o prendere un gelato in uno dei tanti caffè.

data.name: Venice Evening Food Tour in Cannaregio with Authentic Sit-Down Dinner
data.description: You’ll meet near Venice’s famous the Teatro Italia where your food-obsessed, English-speaking guide will be waiting. Along with a group of up to 10 people, you’ll explore the side streets of the Cannaregio district, visiting one of our favorite bacari wine bars, sampling assorted cicchetti dishes, and tasting some of finest regional food and wine in Italy. You’ll also enjoy a sit-down meal with your group at one of the city’s best pasta restaurants. This foodie-led exploration of Venetian culture and history shows you a side of the city most tourists won’t see (or taste!).Venice Food Tour DescriptionYour 2.5-hour tour includes:Small plates called cicchettiProsecco, wine, and cocktailsSit-down pasta dinner and gelatoShort walking tour of CannaregioEnglish-speaking, local guideMaximum of 10 people per groupCannaregio and the Jewish QuarterYour evening in Venice is set in the beautiful neighborhood of Cannaregio. Originally a working-class neighborhood, it has become the center of local Venetian cuisine and culture. Along with your local guide, you’ll explore the most populous of Venice's six sestieri or districts.Within Cannaregio, you’ll also visit the Jewish neighborhood from which the word "ghetto" originates. As you explore the small canals and streets, you’ll see a more authentic, less touristy side of Venice that will make you fall in love with the city all over again.Cicchetti and BacariThere are two words that are vital to know when visiting Venice—cicchetti and bacari. The word cicchetti comes from Venetian dialect, meaning "a small savory snack.” They’re served at various bacari (wine bars) and come in many delicious varieties. Traditional bacari date back to at least the 1300s and have become an integral part of life in Venice.Your local Venetian guide will explain the history of bacari and why people visited them during the day (and even in the morning!). When Italians drink wine, they always have something to eat with it to make sure that they don't get too tipsy. So over time, the bacari started offering cicchetti and a new tradition was born: drinking wine with cicchetti.The SpritzWhether you have a sweet tooth or prefer something bitter, there’s a spritz for everyone. For example the Campari spritz has a higher alcohol content than an Aperol Spritz, and it also tastes more bitter than sweet.The Select Spritz Apertivo-- the original signature Venetian Spritz-- has been a staple in the Venetian lifestyle since the 1920s and is a local favorite.If you’ve ever seen pictures of people in Italy drinking a bright orange cocktail in a stemmed glass, that’s an Aperol spritz. Both drinks are made with prosecco. data.name: Valpolicella and Amarone Private Tour from Venice with Sommelier
data.description: A gourmet tour discovering the soul of Valpolicella, the excellent wine and the beautiful landscapes from the vineyards to the Lake Garda, with a certified FISAR Sommelier that will introduce in the ​unique panorama of the Italian Wines. You can decide to visit the Valpolicella area + Garda Lake, or only Valpolicella area, with 2 visits​ in the wineries and wine tastings.

data.name: Guided Walking Tour to The Haunted Paths of Venice
data.description:
Join us for an unforgettable exploration of Venice's hidden secrets on our guided walking tour. As you wander through the city's winding streets and mysterious squares, your knowledgeable guide will share tales of mystery, murder, and superstition that have long captivated locals and visitors alike.

This tour offers a unique perspective on Venice, taking you to areas that are often overlooked by tourists. Explore hidden squares and dimly lit alleys, discovering a side of the city that comes alive after dark. Through the historic Castello district, you'll learn about the fascinating history of Venetian doges and noblemen, gaining insights into the city's storied past.

Listen as stories unfold of unrequited love, ghostly apparitions outside the Malibran Theater, and tragic deaths that have left their mark on Venice's streets.

data.name: Negozio Olivetti Guided Tour
data.description:
Boost your appreciation of Venice with this special guided tour by staff from the National Trust for Italy. An expert guide will lead to way, to discover a hidden gem in St. Mark's Square designed by Carlo Scarpa.

The Olivetti Showroom in St Mark's Square was built by the Venetian architect Carlo Scarpa (1906-1978), who designed this dazzling showroom in quite an eclectic style! Wander around the ornamental fountain and check out the vintage typewriters. Get your head around the staircase with strangely offset sections, and see how your shoes look against the blue Murano glass squares on the floors.

It's a stark and peaceful contrast to St. Mark's Square, roaring outside the windows.

data.name: Mask Workshop - Paint your own mask
data.description: Create your own unique Venetian mask at our mask-painting workshop. Paint your mask using acrylic tempera paints of different colors, and then add finishing touches with feathers, ribbons, sequins.... Under the guidance of our artist, you’ll choose a mask from more than 50 different models all handmade in papier maché and decorate it according to different techniques. You will be guided through each of the steps of decorating your mask, including the final touch - gold and silver metallic paints which will bring something more on your wonderful mask. At the end, you will take home your decorated mask together with this wonderful experience

data.name: Artisanal Ice Cream Workshop in Venice
data.description: Make gourmet ice cream from scratch at a private Venice cooking class, and learn how Italian ice cream goes from fresh milk to the delicious finished product. In addition to making your own batch of artisanal ice cream, you’ll sample a range of ice creams and sorbets in a variety of styles.

data.name: Dining experience at a local's home in Murano with cooking demo
data.description: There's no better way to discover Italy's culture from the inside. Our national network of expert Italian home cooks offers the finest Italian food experiences. Immerse yourself in a private dining experience with an Italian family with a 4-course menu (starter, pasta, main course and dessert with drinks included: water, selection of local wines and coffee) showcasing authentic Italian recipes passed down by real Italian Mammas in family cookbooks. Enjoy a cooking demonstration, where your host will show you their cooking skills as they finish the dishes in front of you. Feel the warmth of Italian hospitality by connecting with local people. You'll come away with happy memories, new friends, and a deeper understanding of your destination, as you taste the typical dishes that real Italians cook every day. This experience is held by Cesarine, the oldest Italy’s network of home cooks available all over the country. The word "Cesarine" means "home cook". Our network of passionate and welcoming local hosts open the doors of their own homes to curious travellers for immersive culinary experiences. The Cesarine serve only local specialties from their family cookbooks to tell the great story of their traditional regional cuisine.

data.name: Venice Street Food and Sightseeing Walking Tour
data.description: This full immersion into the Venetian Street Food scene takes 2.5 hours and start near the Rialto Bridge. To begin this fun and delicious street food tour be ready to taste all the local specialties. Explore the busy Rialto Market to see colorful stalls selling seafood, vegetables, and fruit. Throughout your tour, see some of the main sights of the city, including the Campo San Bartolomeo, Campo San Polo, Basilica dei Frari, and more. Taste some of Venice's local specialties, such as the bite-sized cicchetti served at bars all over the city. These tapas-like snacks are popular with Venetians who meet friends after work for a drink and a few bites before dinner. Sample cheese made in the region, traditional cakes, buranelli biscuits and much more! Take this tour early in your Venice visit to reap the rewards of all you'll learn about where to go and what to eat in the canal city.

data.name: Authentic 3-Course Venetian Dinner with Wine Pairing and Murano Glass Gift
data.description: Enjoy an authentic and intimate culinary experience in the heart of Venice with this seasonal three-course dinner hosted in a private Venetian home. Perfect for food lovers and culture seekers, this experience offers a taste of Italy beyond the restaurants—served with warm local hospitality and attention to detail. Start your evening with a Prosecco welcome and warm homemade focaccia, paired with a tasting of EVO Nativo, a private-label Sicilian olive oil. The appetizer features a savory green asparagus flan with salicornia cream and grilled shrimp. A vegetarian alternative with creamy pecorino fondue and walnuts is also available. For the main course, handmade tagliatelle are gently risottata-style with a velvety purple artichoke sauce and crispy guanciale—or a lighter version with fresh chives and dill for vegetarians. A refreshing lemon sorbet with white vodka and mint acts as a pre-dessert, followed by a bold and balanced final course: a creamy basil dessert on 70% dark chocolate crumble, garnished with fresh fruit. The evening includes one bottle of natural wine for every three guests (your choice of Prosecco Brut or Còvolo red), artisanal bread, mineral water, espresso, and a sip of homemade limoncello to close. To make the evening even more special, every guest receives a unique Murano glass perolo—a vibrant handcrafted paperweight to take home as a piece of Venice. Minimum booking: 4 guests. Ideal for couples, families, and small groups looking for a refined yet personal food experience in Venice.

data.name: Venice Private Transfer: Luxury Travel to Canazei
data.description: Travel in style from either Venice Marco Polo Airport (VCE) or Piazzale Roma (the city’s land-side transportation hub) to your hotel, apartment or other address in Canazei or the surrounding area. You’ll enjoy “Meet and Greet” service from your professional, English-speaking driver before setting off towards the Dolomites in an air-conditioned luxury van or sedan.

data.name: Essential Venice Private Tour: Highlights of the Floating City
data.description: A jaw-dropping treasure trove of art and culture, the charms of Venice could easily occupy you for a lifetime. But if you’re new to the Floating City and want to get straight to the highlights, then our Essential Venice tour offers the perfect introduction to the city known to history as the Serenissima. On our itinerary we’ll be visiting the two greatest landmarks in Venice, with skip-the-lines access: iconic Saint Mark’s basilica, with its glittering mosaics, and the no less spectacular Doge’s Palace - symbol of Venice’s limitless power for nearly a millennium and home to the breathtaking Bridge of Sighs. Afterwards head off in search of hidden corners of Venice that few visitors get to see in the company of our local expert. This is Venice at its authentic, spectacular best!

data.name: Rialto Market Tour and Cooking Class in Palazzetto Pisani
data.description: Immerse yourself in a unique and unforgettable culinary adventure at the exquisite Palazzetto Pisani Gran Canal in Venice. This enriching experience begins with a visit to the iconic Rialto Market, renowned for its vibrant atmosphere and an abundance of fresh, seasonal ingredients. Here, you'll explore stalls brimming with colorful produce and freshly caught seafood, learning how to select the best ingredients while soaking in the aromatic scents and lively energy of this historic marketplace. Following the market tour, you'll make your way to Palazzetto Pisani, a stunning historic home that offers breathtaking views of the Grand Canal. In this elegant setting, you'll step into a well-equipped kitchen where expert chefs will guide you through a hands-on cooking class. This is not just a demonstration; you'll be actively involved in the preparation of two authentic recipes: fresh pasta and a delectable dessert. With all the necessary ingredients and utensils at your disposal, you'll learn traditional techniques and tips to create these Italian specialties from scratch. Once the cooking is complete, the experience continues with a delightful tasting session. You'll have the opportunity to savor the fruits of your labor, enjoying the dishes you’ve prepared in a convivial and relaxed atmosphere. The meal is complemented by unlimited still and sparkling water, as well as a generous provision of wine (one bottle for every two guests) to enhance your dining experience. To finish, enjoy a cup of coffee, rounding off your culinary journey in true Italian style. This exceptional experience at Palazzetto Pisani offers more than just a cooking lesson; it provides a deep dive into Venetian culture and culinary traditions. Whether you are a seasoned cook or a beginner, this immersive adventure promises to be a highlight of your visit to Venice, leaving you with not only new skills but also lasting memories of a truly special day.

data.name: Venice: Skip-the-line St. Mark's Basilica Entry & Audioguide
data.description:
Skip-the-Line Ticket to St. Mark’s Basilica with Audio Guide + Optional Upgrades

Skip the lines and step into the breathtaking beauty of Venice’s most iconic landmark — St. Mark’s Basilica. With your fast-track ticket and included audio guide, explore the glittering golden mosaics, marble floors, and rich history of this Byzantine masterpiece at your own pace.

Discover the secrets behind centuries of art and devotion as you admire the basilica’s soaring domes and ornate chapels — all brought to life through your multilingual audio guide.

Perfect for independent travelers who want maximum flexibility and insight — all with zero time wasted in line. Book now and unlock the full magic of St. Mark’s Basilica.

data.name: Cortina & the Dolomites in 1 day from Venice by private car
data.description: Enjoy a memorable day tour discovering Europe’s most beautiful mountains: the Italian Dolomites. With this tour you will see in one day directly from Venice the most famous towns and lakes in the dramatic Dolomite Mountains: Pieve di Cadore, Tre Cime di Lavaredo, Cortina, Lake Misurina, Lake Auronzo. Our first stop will be Cortina d'Ampezzo, where customers could visit the town and have lunch in one of the excellent restaurants of the city or take the Cortina-Faloria cable car to fully appreciate the beauty of the Ampezzo Dolomites. The second stop will be Lake Misurina, a fraction of Cortina and a lovely place for a walk in the open air, in a setting of great charm. The Lake Misurina, known also as the pearl of the Dolomites" is one of the most beautiful Italian lakes. As well as for its charm, it is also known for its therapeutic properties thanks to its particularly healthy microclimate. A legend has it that, the lake was a gift from the fairy of Mount Cristallo to the daughter of King Sorapiss, Misurina, who insistently wanted a magic mirror. The mirror (of water) was given to the girl but only on one condition: the king shoudl be turned into an imposing mountain, and thus explained the formation of the Sorapiss mountain group and the splendid lake. The following stop will be Tre Cime di Lavaredo, an extraordinary and privileged "terrace" of the natural park, from which it is possible to admire the entire panorama of the Dolomites. You can visit the galleries dug into the mountain like trenches during the world war. Our last stop will be the Lake of Auronzo, also known as the Lake St. Catherine. It is a wonderful artificial lake where you can relax before returning to Venice. N.B: THE ITINERARY MAY VARY ACCODING TO THE SNOW OR WEATHER CONDITIONS

data.name: St. Mark’s Basilica: Guided Tour With Pala D'oro Access
data.description: Explore St. Mark's Basilica on a guided tour blending Eastern and Western architectural styles. Discover Venice's history, including Saint Mark's relics and the Basilica's golden mosaics and marble inlays. Learn about the history and look at the Pala d'Oro, a Byzantine masterpiece altar adorned with gold, silver, and precious stones, housing Saint Mark's remains.

data.name: Verona in 1 day from Venice
data.description: In the morning, reach Venice railway station on your own and get on the speed train that will take you to Verona in just 1 hour and a half. You will meet your guide at Verona's railway station where you will start your 2-hour guided tour. You will take a relaxing walk through the picturesque and full of history street of Verona, the so called "city of love". Here indeed, the most famous and tragic denouement of history of the two lovers - Romeo & Juliet - by the writer William Shakespeare took place. You will see Juliet's balcony, where -it's said- she looked out to see her lover Romeo; the lucky statue of Juliet, Romeo's House, Piazza dei Signori, Porta Borsari where the duel took place between Capuleti and Montecchi, the famous Arena, where all the most famous concerts are still held every year. You will then have some free time to enjoy the city and spend some time at your pace to make some shopping, taste the famous "Juliet's braid", a typical dessert of Verona, or sip a glass of Valpolicella, a wonderful red wine coming from the famous namesake hill of Verona. In the early evening reach Verona railway station and get on your train for your trip back to Venice. Arrival in Venice railway station at 7.00pm approximately. Departure from Venice: train RV leaves at 8.10am from Santa Lucia Venice railway station (arrival in Verona Porta Nuova at 9.38am) Departure from Verona: train RV leaves at 5.22pm from Verona Porta Nuova railway station (arrival in Santa Lucia Venice at 6.50pm)

data.name: St. Mark’s Essentials: Basilica, Doge's Palace & Bell Tower
data.description: Step into the heart of Venice and discover the stories behind its most iconic landmarks. In just one hour, this guided outdoor tour takes you through the majestic St. Mark’s Square, where you'll explore the exteriors of three architectural masterpieces: the Basilica di San Marco, the Doge’s Palace, and the Bell Tower. With the insights of a knowledgeable local guide, you’ll uncover fascinating tales of Venice’s golden age, from the power of the Doges to the symbolism of the Basilica’s ornate façade. As you move through the square, your guide will reveal details that most visitors miss, offering the perfect blend of history, legends, and breathtaking views. This outdoor tour is the perfect introduction to Venice, ideal before visiting the interiors on your own or continuing your exploration through the winding alleys and canals of the city

data.name: Ca' Rezzonico Museum: Guided Tour + Casanova Walking Tour
data.description:
Visit Ca’ Rezzonico, a historic palace on the Grand Canal from the 1700s. See one of the well-preserved baroque palaces in Venice, reflecting the luxurious lifestyle of the Venetian aristocracy during Giacomo Casanova's era.

Walk through halls with original frescoes, crystal chandeliers, antique furniture, and Venetian art. Each room showcases wealth and power in a city that was once one of the richest in Europe.

As you move through the salons, look out at gondolas on the Grand Canal through the windows. Ca’ Rezzonico offers more than a museum visit; it provides a look into Venice’s prosperous past and an important stop for those interested in history and art.

data.name: Venice Mainland to Islands 1-Way Bike Tour with Coffee
data.description: The Liberty Bridge (Ponte della Libertà) links Venice’s mainland industrial downtown (Marghera) with its historic islands and old town. Get a fresh perspective on these two very different environments and enjoy a magical cycle over the lagoon on this small-group bike tour, with a guide to lead the way and point out the attractions. Drop off your bike at Tronchetto Island then discover the old town independently.

data.name: Tour on the Trails of Commissario Brunetti in Venice
data.description: A special itinerary through Venice to discover the places where the Commissioner's numerous films were shot. We will meet Signor Vianello, the unfailing Vice-Petty Officer Patta, Signora Battistini, the wonderful Signorina Elettra, crossing plots, moments and the beautiful Venice.

data.name: VENICE| Private tour with personal photographer from FLORENCE
data.shortDescription:
Meeting point

We will meet the participants at the station of Florence SMN and leave by high-speed train.

 

What will the itinerary be?

We'll arrive in Venice around 12.00. With the Vaporetto (water bus) we'll reach the Rialto Bridge where we'll stop for the first photo-shoot.

You'll have free time for lunch then we'll get to Piazza San Marco by walking. There are dozens of perfect places in the square area to be photographed: in front of the basilica, under the arcades that house the ancient bars, on the pier, or along the Riva Degli Schiavoni, with the Bridge of Sighs in the background and many more.

You will spend more than an hour in the surroundings, and then take the narrow alleys that lead to a magical place in Venice: the Acqua Alta bookshop. This is the most beautiful bookstore in the world or at least the most particular, it offers its visitors a perfect setting for photoshoots. Due to the frequent flooding of the room, the owner is obliged to safeguard its volumes by placing them in basins, gondolas, and other containers raised from the ground. Here we will spend at least an hour, taking pictures and leafing through magazines and then walk calmly towards the station.

You'll have free time for shopping until departure, which will be around 6.00pm. The arrival in Florence will be at approximately 8.00pm.

 

When and how will the photos be sent?

The photoshoot material will be delivered in 48h via WeTransfer or Google Drive.

The photo format will be high quality jpg only.
